answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to earn a nontransferable reputation through repeated, independently sampled tasks, with rewards withheld until several peers verify its work. A Sybil operator must then fund many agents, perform useful tasks, and keep them consistent across checks; merely minting accounts gains no influence. Random audits and penalties for colluding approvals make coordination costly. A reef of reviewers can flag a lotus-pattern of linked behavior, while a quill records the evidence for later challenges.
